Fixed in c739776f. Agreed on the root cause: `resolveAccountApiBaseUrl` prefers the provider `baseUrl`, while the link used `getClineEnvironmentConfig().appBaseUrl`, so a staging override with `CLINE_ENVIRONMENT` unset opened production.

`@cline/shared` now exports `resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`, which maps the resolved backend to the environment that declares it (trailing slash ignored). The CLI resolves the account backend once, passes that exact base URL to `createClineAccountService`, and builds the link from `resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`. A backend no environment declares (proxy, self-hosted) resolves to `undefined`, and `getClinePrivacySettingsUrl` now hides the link in that case instead of opening a different environment.

The same mismatch existed in the desktop sidecar `get_cline_app_base_url`, so it uses the same helper now. Tests: `resolveClineAppBaseUrl` (shared), `loadClineAccountSnapshot` links to `staging-app.cline.bot` for a staging override and hides the link for an unmatched backend, and the sidecar command returns `https://staging-app.cline.bot` / `undefined` likewise.

Please resolve the desktop app URL once at startup from the existing environment configuration and expose it as desktop configuration. We don't support switching the account/backend or environment after startup, so this doesn't need to run on each account refresh. Any startup provider override should be handled in that same configuration resolution. The webview still needs the resolved app URL passed across from the sidecar, but it doesn't need a separate account-driven refresh lifecycle.

the sidecar resolves it once at startup in [`728da6af`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/commits/728da6afab). [`index.ts`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-de4516568662afaa257a93b87322919abf6f8373f618c12105b06ba1f7543271R74) sets `ctx.clineAppBaseUrl` right after `createSidecarContext`, from [`resolveSidecarClineAppBaseUrl()`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-a9c19745939a47e95eaec39bdd97cf7f0bb114576e7d9d389d9a3a527fc6eb88R668) in `context.ts`, which reads the provider `baseUrl` override in that same resolution. `get_cline_app_base_url` [just returns the field](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-bc6a66091bf2af602bcea86b8eafccd68a2cc5a9c52d1c2432207cdcb5e798a2R3226) instead of reading provider settings on every call, and environment-scoped contexts inherit the value. covered by [`returns the app URL resolved at startup, for every environment context`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-3d4567b52dd7fd16627866a2413bc613f7804f496eab4cfa1be309ffb11ad7d9R252).

Suggestion: make the visibility filter unconditional and drop `mcpApps` from `CreateMcpToolsOptions`.

The spec says the host MUST NOT list tools whose visibility doesn't include `"model"`, with no exception for hosts that haven't advertised the apps extension. A tool tagged `visibility: ["app"]` is never meant for the model, so hiding it when apps are off is still the right behavior (there's no app around to call it either).

That leaves the client factory flag as the single switch for MCP Apps, and removes the "the two must be set together" caveat from DOC.md. Conformant servers only send `_meta.ui` tools after the client advertises the capability anyway, so the factory flag is the real gate.

Not blocking, approving as is. It's just cheaper to collapse this now than after the option is in the published `@cline/core` surface. Feel free to make the change and I can re-review.
Hey! I went this way so as not to break the existing interface, but you're right; it's probably better to do so now rather than later.

Valid, and it exposed the real problem: the extension kept its own copy of the SDK's rules for reading a rule's enabled state, and this was the fourth case where the copy disagreed with the SDK. The copy is gone. The Rules panel, both write paths, and the editor now call `parseRuleConfigFromMarkdown` / `parseSkillConfigFromMarkdown` from `@cline/core`, so they cannot disagree with what the SDK loads. A file with non-mapping frontmatter (which the SDK loads as having no metadata) is disabled by adding a `disabled: true` block above it, and re-enabling restores it exactly; a comment-only block gets the flag appended inside it. Tests cover both, plus a scratch property check of ~16k generated shapes against the SDK parser as the oracle with zero refusals of loadable files. A file the SDK does not load at all now shows as off, since nothing from it reaches the model.

agent review: Stepping back from the specific symptom: this makes telemetry configuration mutate real session state. `configure()` returns `{ ...this.config, hooks }`, and `this.config` is the start config _with a minted `sessionId` added_ — so line 177 hands core a config that now says "the caller is resuming a session it already has." Core reads `config.sessionId` as exactly that signal (`wasSessionIdRequested` → `isRestart`, and `isReadOnlyResumeStart`).

"New Task" doesn't notice because it already sets the id upstream. "Edit Message & Regenerate" does — it arrives with the field empty and now emits `task.restarted` for a genuinely new session, plus an unneeded manifest probe. But the two symptoms aren't the point; the point is that an observer shouldn't be able to change what core sees. Anything it adds to `this.config` becomes bootstrap truth.

Suggestion: `configure()` return `{ ...originalConfig, hooks }` — the observer keeps the id in `this.config` for its own map key, and core sees an empty sessionId exactly as before. Telemetry attaches hooks; it doesn't rewrite the input.
